task.description: Final re-check of TEST-DESIGNER's/ELIXIR-DEV's rework after both of TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's prior findings (FK-constraint mapping, pause-seam compile-time gating) were fixed and independently re-passed by REVIEWER (step-02d-reviewer-recheck2.json). acceptance_criteria: AC1 forced-failure test asserts the corrected {:error, {:validation, changeset}} tuple and this is verified against real behavior

result.summary:
Six checks performed. Five pass; one genuine, unaddressed gap found: test/specs/REQ-203.md was never updated after ELIXIR-DEV's rework1 fixed the FK-constraint mapping, so the spec document now directly contradicts both the shipped implementation and the test code it is supposed to describe.

CHECK 1 -- AC1 forced-failure test (activation_test.exs:214-273) -- PASS. Read the test directly: it now asserts `assert {:error, {:validation, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset}} = Activation.activate_group(...)` and `assert {"does not exist", _} = changeset.errors[:active_version_id]` (lines 238, 254), matching activate_group/5's documented @spec and the foreign_key_constraint/3 mapping added to Activation.changeset/2 in commit 6169d009. Ran it myself under MIX_ENV=test: passes.

CHECK 2 -- no stale assert_raise Ecto.ConstraintError left on the FK-mapped path -- PASS. Grepped the whole test file for assert_raise/Ecto.ConstraintError. Three remaining occurrences, all inspected directly and confirmed to test genuinely different, unmapped constraints, not the fixed path: (a) activation_test.exs:501, AC4's test, a raw Repo.insert!/2 bypassing activate_group/5 entirely to prove the UNIQUE(tenant_id, artifact_kind, artifact_name) constraint is DB-enforced -- Activation.changeset/2 has no unique_constraint/3 mapped (by design, per the test's own stated purpose), so Ecto.ConstraintError is the correct, current, expected result; (b)/(c) activation_test.exs:828 and :858, AC9's ON DELETE RESTRICT tests, which call Repo.delete!/1 on an ArtifactVersion struct (a different schema/changeset entirely, with no FK mapping of its own) -- unrelated to the Activation.changeset/2 fix. None of these three needed updating and none were.

CHECK 3 -- full suite -- PASS. Ran myself (not copied): `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/repository/activation_test.exs test/letflow/repository_test.exs test/letflow/repository/canonicaliser_test.exs` -> 'Result: 67 passed', 0 failures, real Postgres.

CHECK 4 -- AC1/AC2 concurrency test under the compile-gated seam -- PASS. The 'AC2 -- concurrent read during an in-flight multi-artifact activation observes no mixed state' test (activation_test.exs:306+) passed as part of the 67/67 run above, confirming @activation_test_hooks_enabled? correctly resolves to true under MIX_ENV=test (config/test.exs sets the flag) so the pause step fires exactly as before the gating was added. Verified directly, not assumed from the flag's dev/prod default.

CHECK 5 -- independent AC8 mutation spot-check -- PASS, performed fresh by me. Edited lib/letflow/repository/activation.ex's resolve/3 nil-branch to fall back to the latest artifact_versions row by version_number instead of returning {:error, :not_activated}. Ran `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/repository/activation_test.exs`: 'Result: 26/28 passed', 2 failures -- confirmed by name: 'AC3 -- per-tenant isolation activating in tenant A does not change tenant B's active version...' and 'AC8 -- resolve/3's not-found semantics never fall back to an arbitrary version resolve/3 returns {:error, :not_activated} when no activation row exists, even though versions DO exist' -- exact match to both TEST-DESIGNER's original report and my own prior independent measurement from step-03b-test-design-validator.json. Reverted with `git checkout -- lib/letflow/repository/activation.ex`; verified with `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` (empty) AND re-ran the suite: 'Result: 28 passed', 0 failures.

CHECK 6 -- implementation diff since last review, narrow/mechanical -- PASS, no new coverage gap. Read `git show 6169d009 -- lib/letflow/repository/activation.ex` (FK-constraint fix) and `git show aa804f61 -- lib/letflow/repository/activation.ex` (pause-seam compile-time gate) in full. Both are exactly the two fixes REVIEWER re-gated: (1) foreign_key_constraint/3 added to Activation.changeset/2 for :active_version_id, plus a documented rationale for why ActivationHistory's own three FKs are unreachable within the same Multi (no new testable surface -- it's a comment, not code); (2) test_opts converted from a public @type to @typep, activate_group/5's public @spec 5th arg changed to plain keyword(), and maybe_add_test_pause_step/3 gated behind @activation_test_hooks_enabled? (an if on a compile-time-constant attribute, not a guard). Neither commit adds any new production behavior needing a new test -- both are narrowing/gating changes to an existing test-only seam, plus a changeset constraint mapping already covered by CHECK 1's test.

GENUINE GAP FOUND -- test/specs/REQ-203.md is stale and now factually wrong: 
1. Item 2 (lines 43-64) still documents AC1's forced-failure test as asserting `assert_raise Ecto.ConstraintError` and states as a 'real finding... for REVIEWER' that the implementation 'surfaces this failure as a RAISED Ecto.ConstraintError... not the returned {:error, {atom(), Ecto.Changeset.t()}} tuple.' This is now false: the implementation was fixed (commit 6169d009) specifically because this mismatch was found blocking at Step 3b, and the test itself (activation_test.exs:238-254) now asserts the corrected tuple. The spec still describes the pre-fix defect as current, shipped behavior.
2. The 'A note on the AC1/AC2 concurrency mechanism' section (lines 18-33) still says 'Flagged for REVIEWER: this is new surface on a file REVIEWER already signed off on' -- REVIEWER has since reviewed and PASSED this exact surface twice (step-02d-reviewer.json PASS, then step-02d-reviewer-recheck2.json final PASS after the compile-time-gating rework). This reads as an open, unresolved flag when it is resolved. The same section also references 'that module's @type test_opts moduledoc' -- test_opts is now @typep, not @type (commit aa804f61), so this cross-reference is also stale.
3. The 'Real Postgres runs performed during test design' section (lines 210-221) documents 'a mid-Multi FK failure that the implementation actually raises differently than initially assumed -- resolved by asserting the real observed exception rather than an invented one' as the FINAL resolution of that finding. That resolution has since been superseded: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's Step 3b FAIL (step-03b-test-design-validator.json) required ELIXIR-DEV to fix the implementation instead of leaving the test matching the raised exception, and that fix shipped. The spec's own narrative of how this finding was resolved is now incorrect.

This is not a coverage gap (every AC still has real, non-vacuous, passing test coverage, confirmed above) and does not block TEST-RUNNER's ability to run the suite -- but test/specs/REQ-203.md is the authoritative AC-to-test-case mapping document this project uses, and per this same run's own routing item 3 in step-03b-test-design-validator.json ('TEST-DESIGNER (Step 3 rework, after 1+2 land): ... update test/specs/REQ-203.md's corresponding entry'), updating this document was already an explicit, agreed part of the rework -- it was simply never done. A document asserting factually incorrect claims about shipped behavior, left in the repository as the AC-to-test authoritative mapping, is exactly the kind of inconsistency this gate exists to catch, and letting it stand only because the underlying test code is correct would mean the spec permanently misdescribes AC1's coverage to any future reader.

CONCLUSION: FAILED. Routing to TEST-DESIGNER to update test/specs/REQ-203.md only (no code or test changes needed -- activation_test.exs itself is fully correct and consistent, confirmed above):
1. Item 2 (lines 43-64): rewrite to describe the CURRENT test, which asserts {:error, {:validation, changeset}} with changeset.errors[:active_version_id] == {"does not exist", _}, and note this was fixed via foreign_key_constraint/3 on Activation.changeset/2 (commit 6169d009), not left as a raised-exception finding.
2. Lines 18-33: remove/update the 'Flagged for REVIEWER... already signed off on' language (REVIEWER has since passed this surface, twice) and correct '@type test_opts' to '@typep test_opts'.
3. Lines 210-221 ('Real Postgres runs performed during test design'): update the FK-failure bullet to reflect the final resolution (implementation fixed, not the test left matching a raised exception), or add a follow-up note referencing this run's step-03b rework.
4. No changes needed to activation_test.exs itself, and no new test cases are required -- re-route straight back to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for a narrow doc-only re-check once the spec file is updated.

All code-level and test-code-level checks (1-6 above) are fully PASSED and do not need to be redone -- only the spec markdown file needs a text update.
